title: API key soft-expiry causes RBAC enforcement inconsistency during Private/Dedicated rolling upgrades
creator: Ava Chen
description: Several Dedicated and Private customers reported intermittent 403 errors for a subset of API calls immediately after scheduled rolling upgrades or capacity pool drains. Errors only appeared for requests signed with recently-rotated API keys (within their grace window). Issue surfaced in VPC/on-prem proxies and in dedicated gateways; Hosted fallback path did not exhibit the same failure mode.
steps_to_repro: Provision a Dedicated pool with dedicated gateway and VPC peering
Create an API key with role bindings and simulate a role change + rotation (rotate server-side key)
Trigger a rolling node drain/upgrade across gateway nodes (simulate drain order)
Replay in-flight requests that are signed with the old key but within the soft-expiry grace window
Observe intermittent 403s on RBAC-protected routes while some other routes continue to accept the same signature
observed_behavior: During rolling drain some gateways accept requests signed with rotated keys but downstream RBAC lookup consults a stale role-binding cache; result: authentication succeeds but authorization lookup returns missing binding -> 403. Errors are non-deterministic across nodes and routes. Customers saw user-facing errors in production and escalated.
expected_behavior: Either fully accept or reject requests under rotation semantics: requests within grace window should have consistent RBAC decisions across the request path. No route-level 403s should appear if the signing and binding states are compatible.
root_cause: TTL mismatch and non-atomic cache invalidation between API key validation layer and the RBAC binding cache during node drain. When a gateway node validated the signature using the rotated key mapping, it forwarded request metadata to an RBAC service instance that had not yet refreshed its binding table, causing a false-negative authorization. The dedicated/Private deployment uses local caching and a shorter propagation channel than Hosted, exposing the race.
mitigation: Hotfix: temporarily extend grace window on signature acceptance to allow full binding propagation (applied to affected customers)
Applied emergency config to serially drain gateways for impacted customers to avoid overlapping cache states
Customer comms: notified affected customers with recommended mitigation and ETA for permanent fix
fix_plan: 1) Ensure cache invalidation is coordinated: introduce a bounded barrier so RBAC cache refresh follows key mapping update with observable acknowledgement
2) Add an atomic rotation handshake: when a key is rotated, mark a short 'rotation-in-progress' state that triggers synchronous binding reload on local RBAC instances
3) Add consistency checks during request handling: if signature validation maps to a role that lookup cannot find, trigger a fast-binding-refetch path before returning 403
4) Write integration tests simulating rolling upgrades with inter-node cache windows and validate no 403s are returned for in-flight grace-window requests
5) Backfill telemetry: surface a new dashboard metric for 'authz-mismatch-after-authn' to detect regressions
qa_notes: Create a staging cluster with same caching topology as Dedicated (local RBAC caches + short propagation)
Run chaos test harness that randomly rotates keys while performing node drains and assert zero user-facing 403s
Add test vectors for function-calling routes and streaming endpoints as they exercise different codepaths
